identity.title: ATOMS: ALMA Three-millimeter Observations of Massive Star-forming regions - XXI. A large-sample observational study of ethanol and dimethyl ether in hot cores
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: The observations were carried out with ALMA band 3 towards 146 Infrared Astronomical Satellite (IRAS) clumps (2019.1.00685.S, PI: Tie Liu).

We present a deep line survey of two isomers of C2H6O: ethanol (C2H5OH; EA), and dimethyl ether (CH3OCH3; DE) as well as their possible precursor CH3OH towards 60 hot cores by using the ALMA 3 mm line observations.

method.value: LTE radiative transfer modeling in XCLASS with source size fixed to deconvolved continuum size, velocity offset referenced to CH3OH 100.6389 GHz line, and manual adjustment of rotation temperature, column density, and line width

Then, three parameters: rotation temperature, column density, and line width are set to be free parameters for fitting the observed spectra using the XCLASS software. The rotation temperature, column density, and line width were manually adjusted to achieve a reasonable match between the synthetic and observed spectra.

analysis_steps.goal: Optimization and error estimation of rotation temperatures and column densities

method.value: Fix line width from Step 1, run MAGIX with Levenberg-Marquardt and MCMC algorithms to optimize Trot and N and derive uncertainties. For sources with only 1-2 lines, assume Trot = 150 K

evidence.quote: - In the second step, the line width is set as a fixed parameter based on the first step. We then employ the Modeling and Analysis Generic Interface for eXternal numerical codes (MAGIX; (cite: 2013A&A...549A..21Moller)) to obtain optimized rotation temperatures and column densities. In the calculation, the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm (LM) and the Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm (MCMC) are employed to estimate the errors in the derived rotation temperatures and column densities.

For sources where only one or two molecular lines of DE and EA were detected, the rotation temperature could not be constrained. We calculated the column densities using three different temperatures (100 K, 150 K, and 200 K), which showed a slight increase in column density, with the variation remaining within 20%. We chose a median value of 150 K to derive their column densities.

claims.hypothesis: Ethanol (EA) and dimethyl ether (DE) share a chemical link connected to CH3OH as a common precursor.
claims.experiment: Observe and derive column densities of EA, DE, and CH3OH across 60 ATOMS hot cores and 28 literature sources, then evaluate their Pearson correlation coefficients and column density ratios.
claims.result: Strong correlations were found between N(EA) and N(DE) (rho = 0.92), N(EA) and N(CH3OH) (rho = 0.82), and N(DE) and N(CH3OH) (rho = 0.80), with the EA/DE ratio remaining within ~1 order of magnitude (0.1-2.1, mean 0.60).
claims.finding: EA, DE, and CH3OH are chemically linked, likely formed via radical-radical recombination involving CH3OH dissociation products on ice mantles.

evidence.quote: These strong correlations and the stable ratios, suggest that EA, DE, and CH3OH could be chemically linked, with CH3OH potentially serving as a precursor for EA and DE.
These correlations and nearly constant ratio hint at a potential chemical link between EA and DE via CH3OH, as suggested by previous experiments and models.

claims.hypothesis: Existing gas-grain chemical models accurately reproduce the observed abundances of C2H6O isomers in hot cores.
claims.experiment: Compare measured column densities and abundances of EA and DE relative to CH3OH with predictions from chemical models with three different warm-up timescales.
claims.result: Chemical models systematically overproduce EA and underproduce DE compared to observational data.
claims.finding: Existing chemical models fail to match the observed EA and DE abundances, indicating missing or inaccurate reaction pathways (e.g., radical products of CH3OH dissociation need inclusion).

evidence.quote: 5. Compared with chemical models, the abundance of EA is systematically overproduced while the abundance of DE is systematically underproduced in chemical models. Our large hot core sample can provide crucial constraints for chemical models.

claims.hypothesis: The column density ratio of EA to DE depends strongly on the local physical environment (e.g., temperature, presence of HII region).
claims.experiment: Examine the EA/DE column density ratio as a function of rotation temperature and source classification (hot cores vs hot corinos, associated vs non-associated with HII regions).
claims.result: The ratios of EA/DE do not show an upward or downward trend with rotation temperature, remaining within ~1 order of magnitude across both hot cores and hot corinos.
claims.finding: The EA/DE ratio does not depend sensitively on the physical environment, supporting dominant production by radical-radical reactions of CH3OH dissociation products.

evidence.loc: 4.2 Implications for the chemistry of EA and DE
evidence.quote: The ratios of EA/DE do not show an obvious upward or downward trend with the rotation temperatures of both EA and DE. The nearly stable ratios suggest that the EA/DE ratio does not depend on the physical environment.

how_they_decided_enough.value: For sources with only 1-2 detected lines where Trot cannot be constrained, testing column densities at 100, 150, and 200 K showed variations within 20%, justifying fixing Trot to 150 K.

limitations_admitted.value: Adopting source sizes from continuum emission may underestimate or overestimate column densities if molecular line emission extent differs from continuum

evidence.quote: It should be noted that in some sources, the molecular line emissions of EA and DE are not well associated with the continuum emissions. In such case, the adopted source sizes from the continuum may lead to an underestimation of molecular column densities if the molecular emission more compact than the continuum emissions and vice versa.

limitations_admitted.value: Band 3 spectral setup lacks low upper level energy (< 35 K) EA transitions with high Einstein A coefficients, requiring observations at other wavelengths to confirm non-detection in Group D sources

evidence.quote: Because we do not cover the transition line of EA with lower upper level energy (<35 K) and higher Einstein A coefficient, observations at other wavelengths are needed to confirm the absence of EA in these sources, where only two emission lines of DE are detected with upper level energies ranging from 10 to 25 K.

referee_caveats_inferred: Assumption of local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) may not hold uniformly across all hot core sub-regions.
Fixing rotation temperature to 150 K for sources with only 1-2 detected lines introduces systematic uncertainty, although bounded to ~20%.
